A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same min-p sampling work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support reliable comparison; no material reading gaps remain.

before.justification: v3 reports original GPQA and GSM8K experiments, human evaluations, and an explicitly original structured creative-writing evaluation in Appendix C.3.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark, human-study, and structured-generation results, with some revised results and additional statistical reporting.

M1.justification: The relative probability threshold, token filtering, renormalized sampling, and Appendix A.1 implementation remain unchanged. The second human study's inference-engine adjustment and Appendix D.2's proposed min-z extension were already present in v3.

E1.justification: Both versions cover GPQA, GSM8K CoT and self-consistency, AlpacaEval creative writing, human story evaluation, and constrained creative generation. No new model-evaluation task or input scenario is established. The expanded adoption survey concerns the same open-source ecosystem.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including temperature-only, top-k, top-p, epsilon, eta, Mirostat, and the additional configurations in Table 7. Despite v5's new explanatory note, Table 7's extra sampling configurations were already included in v3.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a supplementary adoption-assessment procedure using a specified code-search query and manual inspection, beyond the retained curated integration survey. The LLM evaluation protocols are not demonstrably changed: newly identified judges, controls, and configuration counts document existing evaluations rather than establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 adds corroborating analysis of adoption beyond the curated frameworks, reporting over 13,000 matching code files and manual inspection of their relevance. The temperature and threshold ablations, combined-sampler tests, case studies, second human evaluation, and structured-generation analyses already appeared in v3.

E5.justification: Table 7 changes from point estimates alone to reporting 95% confidence intervals for both win-rate measures and per-configuration counts labeled '# runs'. This substantially expands uncertainty reporting for the creative-writing comparison without establishing additional independent replications. Table 4 also changes its italicized significance criterion from p>0.05 to p<0.05, without explaining a reanalysis.

E6.justification: Several creative-writing entries change. In Table 7, temp150_topp_80 changes from 20.00% to 24.21% win rate and from 43.05% to 17.65% length-controlled win rate; other high-temperature top-p scores and output lengths also change. Table 3b's top-p score changes from 50.07 to 50.43. Table 6 updates reported framework stars from 575,800 to 668,000. Most benchmark and human-study results remain unchanged; the PDFs do not explain the experimental basis of the revised scores.

T1.justification: Appendix A.4 corrects the complementary-threshold expression from 'Top-p-1' to '1-top-p'. This is a limited mathematical correction; the worked example, core sampling equations, and Appendix D.2 mathematics remain unchanged, with no new proof or theorem.

C1.justification: The introduction modestly narrows the human-evaluation contribution to showing 'instances where' evaluators prefer min-p. The central claims about the method, high-temperature quality and diversity, generalization across models, and community adoption remain substantively intact.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly emphasizes that diversity ratings concern one fixed triplet per condition and do not measure variation across other possible triplets. Appendix C.2 distinguishes relative high-temperature robustness from optimal absolute quality. Sections 3.4 and A.5 also qualify framework popularity as evidence of availability and potential impact rather than direct usage.

D1.justification: Section 5.2.3 and Table 7 newly identify openchat-3.5-0106, GPT-4 Turbo judging with chain-of-thought prompting, and the fixed temperature-1 standard-sampling baseline. Section 5.2.2 specifies 20 configurations per method for Figure 2. Appendix A.5 supplies the supplementary search query. The implementation code and project access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography contains the same works, and the substantive positioning against prior sampling methods is retained. The added main-text citation to Tajwar et al. refers to work already cited and discussed in v3's Appendix D.

P1.justification: v5 extensively condenses and rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanations, experimental narrative, and human-evaluation discussion. It standardizes terminology and folds the separate resource-availability subsection into Section 3.4. These are substantial editorial changes despite largely stable scientific content; some malformed prose remains.

P2.justification: The existing figures and tables are retained, with several relocated and captions rewritten. Table 6 expands and removes its framework-group headings; Table 7 widens its presentation to include confidence intervals, counts, and an explanatory note. The underlying Figure 1 and Figure 2 graphics remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 improves transparency through Table 7's uncertainty and count reporting, clearer evaluation details, and explicit limits on the human diversity judgments. These gains are tempered by unexplained score revisions and a new traceability problem: Table 3b's top-p score of 50.43 matches Table 7's p=0.98 row, while its caption still specifies p=0.9 or 0.95. The significance-legend reversal is also unexplained. Overall, reporting improves modestly while the method and most supporting evidence remain unchanged.
